Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No right or mechanism for individuals to view/access their data stored in Sudan's ID system has been documented. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms 'Right of data subject to access a copy of their personal data: No law.' The Civil Registry operates without documented citizen data access portals. SudaPass plans are not specific about individual data access rights.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: KYC using the national ID is enabled in Sudan. The UNCDF report confirms 'the police manage the national ID platform, accessible to MNOs for KYC purposes and used by the credit bureau during the credit-scoring process.' Financial institutions use the national ID number for customer identification as required by the AML/CTF Act 2014 and CBOS regulations. However, the UNCDF also notes that full digital e-KYC platforms are yet to be developed, and KYC currently relies largely on physical document checks.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Sudan's constitution (Section 55) protects the right to privacy including correspondence, which provides a general constitutional basis for judicial oversight of identity systems. The general court system can in principle be used to challenge identity-related decisions. However, no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms have been documented. Assessed as 'Yes but not ID-specific' based on general constitutional protections without dedicated mechanisms.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: The 2011 civil registry reform integrated civil registration with the national ID system — registration requires proof of birth/citizenship, and the national identity number is needed to obtain civil documents (birth certificate, marriage certificate). The UN Sudan presentation (2018) confirms the Civil Registry database tracks births, deaths, marriages, divorces for continuous updating. However, the World Bank SFSP project (2020) identifies NCR links to administrative databases as still being strengthened, and fragmentation remains an issue. Partial integration assessed.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Sudan has no formal data sharing rules for the ID system. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms there are 'no laws restricting cross-border transfer' and no requirements for data sharing notifications, data processing registers, or related frameworks. The UNCDF payment infrastructure report notes the police manage the national ID platform accessible to MNOs for KYC without mention of structured data sharing rules.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Sudan has no data protection legislation. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms: 'Sudan currently has no data protection legislation, although various sectoral laws are of relevance, such as the Electronic Transactions Act 2007, Cybercrime Act 2018, Cybercrime Prevention (Amendment) Act 2020, and Law No. 14 on Information Technology Crime.' A Draft Data Protection Bill was proposed in 2018 but remained in draft form as of research date.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Sudan has no Data Protection Authority. The Data Protection Africa fact sheet confirms: 'no data protection authority yet appointed'. While the National Information Center (NIC) oversees some data-related matters and three new digital authorities were established in November 2025 (Digital Transformation Authority, Sudan Data and AI Authority, Cybersecurity Authority), none functions as a formal DPA with individual rights enforcement powers.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The national ID card and national identity number issued under the Civil Registration Act 2011 serve as legal proof of identity in Sudan. The ID card is required for formal employment (Article 27.3), opening bank accounts, obtaining passports, and other legal purposes. The US State Department and IRB Canada confirm the national ID card/number is the primary legal identity document.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Sudan has a legal framework for its identity system. The Civil Registration Act 2011 mandates civil registration, assignment of the national identity number, and obliges citizens over 16 to obtain an ID card. The Electronic Transactions Act 2007 and Cybercrime Act 2018 provide additional legal underpinning for digital identity activities.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The civil registry is managed domestically by the General Directorate of Civil Registration (Ministry of Interior). However, the payment infrastructure involves Gemalto's Mobile Payment Platform (GMPP) operated by Electronic Banking Services (EBS), indicating some foreign vendor involvement in ID-adjacent systems. The new SudaPass system has not yet disclosed its technology vendor. Assessed as partial in-country maintenance given mixed domestic/foreign components.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance and Economy oversees the Sudan Family Support Program (SFSP), which uses the national civil registry identity platform for digital delivery of cash transfers. The World Bank Sudan Family Support Project (2020) describes the Ministry of Finance's role in the program linked to national ID. However, no comprehensive evidence of full Ministry of Finance oversight of the ID system itself was found.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Sudan's civil registry records fingerprints from all applicants aged 12+ and facial photos at enrollment. The Civil Registration Act 2011 mandates in-person registration with fingerprint recording. The new SudaPass platform is planned to use facial biometrics (face recognition via passport/selfie). Iris scans are not documented as part of the standard system. Classified as 'Facial/Iris' tier (value=3) based on fingerprints + facial photo at minimum.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Sudan introduced a new electronic and centralised civil registry in 2011, replacing the old hand-written and decentralised registers. The database is digital and centrally managed by the General Directorate of Civil Registration under the Ministry of Interior. Each citizen receives a unique 11-digit national identity number linked to biometric data stored digitally.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Sudan's civil registry database is used by ID and passport offices for verification via the national identity number, and the police manage the national ID platform accessible to MNOs and the credit bureau for KYC. However, multiple sources describe registries as fragmented with ministries using different identifiers and humanitarian agencies running parallel databases. The WEF (2026) notes 'registries remain fragmented' and the UNCDF (2023) notes 'CBOS could enhance interoperability between separate systems'. Full system interoperability has not been achieved.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The national ID number is required (mandatory) to open a bank account in Sudan. The Landinfo (2023) report and IRB Canada confirm the national identity card/number is required for banking. The UNCDF (2023) report confirms KYC for financial services relies on the national ID number, and the IRB Canada source explicitly states 'identity cards are required...except for some circumstances such as posting bail and opening a bank account.'

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The ID card in Sudan involves fees. The Landinfo (2023) report notes that the ID card is 'expensive to obtain' with many Sudanese choosing not to get one and instead using other official documents containing their national identity number. The UNCDF Sudan payment infrastructure report confirms the NID card is mandatory but the application process involves costs. The new SudaPass digital platform is announced as free (Ministry of Digital Transformation confirmed it 'shall be free'), but this refers to the new system not yet deployed.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under the Civil Registry Act 2011, ID cards are issued to Sudanese citizens over 16. The Landinfo (2023) report and IRB Canada (2013) confirm mandatory ID card acquisition at age 16 (Article 27.1). Children under 16 can be registered in the civil registry (birth registration), but the ID card itself requires age 16+. Fingerprints recorded from age 12. Scored as '>17' = 1, but clarification: the threshold is 16, which falls in the '>17' equivalent zone since enrollment for the physical ID credential starts at 16.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Under the Civil Registration Act 2011 (Article 27.1), every Sudanese citizen must obtain an identity card at age 16 — it is mandatory by law. The UNHCR Khartoum representative and lawyers cited by IRB Canada confirm this. In practice enforcement varies, but the legal status is mandatory for all citizens over 16.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The IRB Canada source (citing the Sudanese Embassy official) states that 'national identity cards are not required to access public health care, and patients can provide their nationality cards if requested.' This suggests the national ID/nationality card is accepted but not strictly mandatory for healthcare. Scored as 'Accepted not mandatory' based on this evidence.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: The Civil Registry Act 2011 (Article 34.2) provides for an 'alien's identity card' for foreigners residing in Sudan. UNHCR Khartoum representative confirmed registered South Sudanese in Khartoum were issued identification cards by the aliens department and police. However, the national identity number and full national ID are for Sudanese citizens only. Some non-nationals (registered aliens, refugees with UNHCR registration) can get a form of ID.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: According to the IFC report, the national civil registry includes 33 million unique names representing 75-80% coverage (among the highest in Africa). The Landinfo (2023) report cites 82% in 2016 and 35.5/40 million (88.75%) in 2021 per government officials. Conflict and displacement since April 2023 (civil war) may have reduced effective coverage. IFC notes expansion to 90% was planned under SFSP. The 75-80% figure from IFC most credibly represents pre-conflict coverage — scored as 50-69% given post-conflict disruption, or conservatively at 3 (50-69%). Given 2021 official data of ~88%, and accounting for the 2023+ crisis, a value of 3 (50-69%) to 4 (70-89%) is defensible; scored 3 (50-69%) to be conservative given ongoing conflict impacts.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration is mandatory in Sudan. A 2021 study cited by GNI confirmed SIM card registration is mandatory in Sudan. The PikaSim eSIM provider confirms 'Sudan requires national ID or passport registration for all SIM cards.' The uqudo report references Telecommunications and Post Regulatory Authority (TPRA) requirements for SIM registration. MNOs access the national ID platform for KYC per the UNCDF report.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The Sudan Family Support Program (SFSP), a major World Bank-supported cash transfer program targeting 80% of the population (6.5 million families), uses the National Civil Registry identity platform for beneficiary validation and digital delivery of payments. The World Bank Project Appraisal Document (2020) confirms NCR validation is mandatory for SFSP registration. Additionally, formal employment requires a national ID number (Civil Registry Act 2011, Article 27.3).
